# Saturated lattice-free facet witnesses form an empty polytope
facet witnesses. It does not classify empty polytopes and does not
supply an OC depth bound.

Let L be a full-dimensional lattice-free polyhedron in R^n, n>=1,
with irredundant facets F_1,...,F_m. For each i choose

    p_i in Z^n intersect relint(F_i).

Here lattice-free means int(L) intersect Z^n is empty. The polyhedron
may be unbounded. Put P=conv{p_1,...,p_m}.

Then each p_i is a vertex of P, and

    P intersect Z^n = {p_1,...,p_m}.                 (1)

Moreover the witnesses have pairwise distinct parities, so m<=2^n.
If m=2^n, they represent every parity exactly once.

Proof. In an irredundant facet description L={a_j.x<=b_j}, the
relative-interior witness p_i has equality exactly at index i and
strict inequality at every other facet index. Thus p_i cannot be a
convex combination of the other witnesses: their i-th inequalities
are all strict. This proves the vertex assertion.

Every convex combination using at least two distinct witnesses with
positive coefficients satisfies EVERY facet inequality strictly.
For any fixed index j, at least one of those witnesses is different
from p_j and has strict j-th inequality. Therefore that combination
belongs to int(L) and cannot be an integer point. Every point of P
other than its listed vertices has such a representation, proving
(1). If two witnesses had the same parity, their midpoint would be
an integer point of int(L), again impossible.

An additional claim sometimes suggested by the equality m=2^n is
that P must have lattice width one. That claim is NOT established
here. The parity argument alone does not give an integer functional
taking only two consecutive values on the witnesses. It also does
not show that the original mixed body's base projection has width
one, even if such a witness functional were subsequently found.
Those are separate structural and transfer obligations.
# Subsequent width classification check

The contemplated implication from saturation to lattice width one is false.
See `candidate 067c3a013000fe6d` for the
exact 16-vertex, width-two, four-dimensional example, including its
realization by genuine lattice-free facet witnesses. This does not affect
the elementary emptiness and parity statements below; it blocks a width-one
reduction from those statements alone.
